chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Henna increases the water (juice/sap) of the face and increases grey hair.

key_terms.مَاءِ الْوَجْهِ: Water of the face (referring to moisture, juice, or sap)

ai.seo_question: What are the physical effects of applying henna on the face and hair according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the physiological effects of henna, noting that it increases moisture in the face while promoting grey hair. This reflects the traditional understanding of henna as a cooling agent that nourishes the skin but may accelerate the greying process, a view often discussed in classical Shia medical and jurisprudential texts regarding personal grooming and purity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The (application of) henna increase in the water of the face, and frequents the greying’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Applying hair dye with henna increases the beauty of the face as well as gray hairs.”’
